_readme: The subject of the benchmark. `scripts/evaluate.py --model` defaults to `current.hf_model`,
so 'evaluate the model' has one unambiguous answer and a comparison always names what it
This file is DATA, not a claim of quality in the abstract. `reason` states what the
designation rests on, `evidence` says where to check it, and `qualification` states what
the designation does NOT mean. Change it in a deliberate commit that cites new evidence --
never as a side effect of a run, and never by a script. Nothing in this repo writes it.
`hf_model` is `artifacts/hf-tt-tnt-1024` -- ONE fixed directory that gets overwritten with
whatever the current best idea for this size is, rather than a new suffixed sibling per
experiment. See CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-29 consolidation entry. The raw training checkpoints
under artifacts/checkpoints-* are untouched by that convention -- only the derived,
cheaply-regeneratable HF conversions are collapsed to one.
RESOLVED 2026-08-29: an earlier version of this file flagged a confirmed Q&A regression in
a 2048-context retrain. That retrain has been reverted and the 512-context dialogue weights
republished. The regression notice is gone because the regression is gone, not because it
was decided to be unimportant -- see `qualification` for what the episode leaves behind.

current.label: tt-tnt-1024
current.reason: The 512-context dialogue-slice weights (10,764 steps, one epoch over tokens-v4), now shipping a chat template baked into tokenizer_config.json that caps rendered conversation history at the last 5 messages. This pairing is the point: the guard -- not a larger context -- is what prevents the growing-conversation KV-cache crash that is a generic tt-metal/vLLM defect (reproduced identically on stock meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct; docs/upstream-tt-metal-asks.md entry 6). Measured directly at 512 context, the exact crash condition: 14 growing turns, zero crashes, prompt_tokens plateauing at ~102 while messages sent grew to 27, against a hard engine crash at turn 3 before the guard existed. These weights answer questions in form and sometimes in fact ('The color of the sky is blue' outright; 'The city of Turin is the capital of the Province of Turin' -- grammatical, on-topic, factually off), where every 2048-context checkpoint trained returned circular or looping non-answers.
current.qualification: Not unqualified. These are the SAME weights this project designated on 2026-08-18, with a chat template added -- no training improved them, and their known regression stands: 4-gram repeat rate worse than tt-tnt-1024a at 3.32x the seed floor, visible in plain output ('the sky is blue because it is blue because it is blue'), and the spider-legs question still returns a repetition loop. What changed on 2026-08-29 is that a 2048-context replacement was trained, published, measured to be WORSE at question answering, and reverted -- so this designation is a restoration, not an advance. The reason 2048 degraded Q&A was NOT isolated: the epoch-inflation hypothesis (steps held at 10,764 while seq_len quadrupled, taking epochs 1.00 -> 4.00) was tested by a six-checkpoint epoch sweep and NOT supported -- termination came back non-monotone and every comparison against this checkpoint was NOT SIGNIFICANT at n=32, and the metrics chosen carried no signal at all. The discriminating evidence is Q&A coherence, which was READ rather than scored, and the 512-vs-2048 comparison is confounded by epochs and sequence length moving together. Anyone re-raising the context should treat the mechanism as open and should not assume fewer epochs fixes it. Separately: this is a 512-window model, so its loss is not comparable to tt-tnt-v3's 2048-window figure -- evaluate() windows at cfg.seq_len, and comparing across windows is the error this file exists to prevent.

corpus.note: The blend these weights trained on. docs/corpus_blend.md now describes a LATER, re-weighted twelve-source blend (sha 074129b2...) that no published model has trained on and that measured as a null -- see docs/measurements/window-purity-control.md. Recorded here because a corpus generation is not implied by a model size or a training recipe, and this repo has already shipped a checkpoint trained on the wrong one.
